title: Light Computer Applications — Overview and definition
body: Public edition. Public physics and engineering knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. Light computers excel where light is the natural carrier: massive parallelism (many wavelengths at once), matrix math at light speed, and signal processing without conversion. The killer app emerging today is AI acceleration — optical neural networks performing matrix-vector multiplications as light passes through modulator arrays, demonstrated by multiple research groups and startups. Applications cluster around linear algebra, optimization, imaging, and secure communication.

title: Light Computer Applications — Optical neural network acceleration
body: Public edition. Public physics and engineering knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. A neural network layer is mostly matrix multiplication, and optics does it superbly: encode the input vector on modulators, the weights on a modulator array or photonic mesh, and the output appears at the detectors after one pass — at light speed, with energy per multiply far below electronics. Demonstrations reach tera-operations per second in single devices. Training still happens digitally, but inference — the deployed, repeated work — is the optical sweet spot.

demo.title: Ising machine finds the min cut
demo.code: const w=[[0,3,1],[3,0,2],[1,2,0]];let best=1e9;for(let m=1;m<7;m++){const s=[0,1,2].map(i=>(m>>i)&1?1:-1);let cut=0;for(let i=0;i<3;i++)for(let j=i+1;j<3;j++)if(s[i]!==s[j])cut+=w[i][j];if(cut<best)best=cut;}J({min_cut:best});assert(best===3,'ising');

title: Light Computer Applications — Coherent Ising machines and optimization
body: Public edition. Public physics and engineering knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. A coherent Ising machine is a network of optical parametric oscillators whose phases settle into the lowest-loss configuration — which encodes the solution to a combinatorial optimization problem (scheduling, routing, portfolio). Built and demonstrated in Japan and the US, these are real machines solving real 100,000-variable problems. The light computer's optimization app is this technology, productized: state the problem, let the oscillators settle, read the answer.

title: Light Computer Applications — Native optical image processing
body: Public edition. Public physics and engineering knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. Images are light already, so a light computer processes them without conversion: lens-based Fourier filtering (a century-old technique called optical correlators, once used for missile guidance), holographic pattern matching, and edge detection by phase contrast. A correlator finds a target pattern in a scene at light speed — the frame rate is limited only by the SLM refresh. Machine vision front-ends are the natural deployment: camera in, answers out, no digitizer in between.

title: Light Computer Applications — Photonic quantum simulation
body: Public edition. Public physics and engineering knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. Photonic circuits are also a leading quantum computing platform: single photons through beam-splitter meshes perform boson sampling and linear-optical quantum gates (demonstrated by multiple groups, including claimed quantum advantages). The light computer's quantum app simulates molecules and materials by mapping their quantum behavior onto photonic circuits. Classical photonic computing and quantum photonic computing share the same hardware base — one machine, two regimes.

title: Light Computer Applications — Secure communication and QKD
body: Public edition. Public physics and engineering knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. Quantum key distribution (QKD) uses single photons to share encryption keys with eavesdropping detection guaranteed by physics — deployed in metropolitan networks in China, Europe, and the US. The light computer's comms app integrates QKD natively: its lasers and detectors are already the right hardware. Post-quantum cryptography runs on the classical side. Security is thus a built-in application, not an add-on.

demo.title: Quantization error shrinks with bits
demo.code: function err(bits){const q=Math.pow(2,bits);let e=0;for(let i=0;i<100;i++){const x=i/100;e+=Math.pow(x-Math.round(x*q)/q,2);}return e;}const e4=err(4),e8=err(8);J({e4:+e4.toFixed(4),e8:+e8.toFixed(5)});assert(e8<e4,'quant');

title: Light Computer Applications — The light-app developer's path
body: Public edition. Public physics and engineering knowledge, fact-checked reference. Speculative material is absent from this edition; anything not yet established science lives in the Signature twin. Developers program the light computer through frameworks that map familiar operations (matrix multiply, convolution, Fourier transform) onto photonic primitives. The toolchain handles the hard parts: wavelength assignment, loss budgeting, and calibration. The teaching ladder runs from 'light a modulator and read the detector' to 'deploy a trained optical neural network'. Every app ships with its optical program, accuracy characterization, and power budget — analog honesty, always.
